newsitem.title: USA: Atlas completes purchase of Bolivian mines.
newsitem.headline: Atlas completes purchase of Bolivian mines.

text.p: Atlas Corp said Wednesday it has completed the acquisition of Arisur Inc, which owns and operates the Andacaba and the Don Francisco silver, zinc and lead mines located in southern Bolivia.
Atlas said it acquired Arisur from Arimetco International Inc and a group of investors for $3.0 million cash and 4.0 million Atlas common shares.
The Andacaba silver, zinc and lead mine has been in operation since the early 1900's.
An expansion of Andacaba's mining and milling operations is already underway.
When completed in early 1997, mill production is expected to increase to 400 metric tonnes per day from 220.

Atlas said the milling facilities at Andacaba will also be used to process the silver/zinc ore from Don Francisco, which started production in June 1996 and is anticipated to achieve its design capacity of 200 tonnes per day during 1997. It is expected that by 1998 annual metal production from the Andacaba and Don Francisco will be 1.2 million ounces silver, 17,400 tonnes of zinc and 2,700 tonnes of lead.
In addition to these acquisitions, Atlas said, it has negotiated two options to acquire other mining properties and processing facilities for both precious and base metals located in Bolivia.

Atlas said Mario Caron and H. R. Shipes have been appointed to its board of directors. Caron has over 20 years of underground mining experience internationally. Shipes is the chief executive officer of Arimetco.

"With these acquisitions, Atlas will achieve two of its immediate goals: the return of the company to operating status and the acquisition of properties generating positive cash flow," the company said. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610
